Second, the <term>mark of continuity</term> <gloss>pravrtti-laksana</gloss> relies upon wisdom, therefore, it generates feelings of suffering and happiness, giving rise to corresponding, uninterrupted thoughts.

In the second, "continuity," the phrase "relies upon wisdom" clarifies the basis of its arising. This means that based on the previously discriminated objects, one produces feelings of pleasure from beloved objects and feelings of suffering from unbeloved objects. Because one repeatedly initiates thoughts, this continuity appears before the mind. This explains the self-continuity. Furthermore, it can give rise to afflictions, nourish karma, and sustain the cycle of birth and death, thereby causing the continuity of others. The later text says "abiding in and sustaining suffering and happiness, etc." Thus, it says "generating [suffering and happiness]... even to the point of being uninterrupted."

Third, the <term>mark of attachment</term> <gloss>graha-laksana</gloss> means that regarding the previously mentioned objects of suffering and happiness, one fails to understand their emptiness and deeply initiates grasping.

<summary>This passage defines the second and third marks of the six coarse defilements: the continuity of repetitive mental states driven by pleasure and pain, and the erroneous attachment to those states as real.</summary>
<keywords>mark of continuity, mark of attachment, suffering, happiness, karma, birth and death, grasping</keywords>
